# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura agent | boot + triage under an interrupted morning (s39) | 1 | 1.00 | 1.0 | **08-17 — 20 minutes of reading killed two non-fixes before anyone built them.** Kam launched and wrapped it himself (reboot morning); queue deliberately unstarted. Measured the board before reading my figure (136, predicate stated). Caught that my C-5 row named ONE service where the defect lives in TWO (auth + originate `email.ts`), and that my F-9 row's `:595` uncomment sits in a wholly commented-out block while the LIVE nginx block carries no CSP at all — both rows would have closed tickets while changing nothing. Archived 14 Done with a control proving the zero; extranet left un-marked-seen with the reason stated. Queue re-issued to s40 with its corrections folded in verbatim. |
| NexusAI agent | deploy gate under coordinator silence | 1 | 1.00 | 1.0 | **08-17 — held the authorised RD-95+98 demo deploy because RD-94 is an inseparable git ancestor, and silence may not resolve a scope question permissively.** Both asks were right (ride-along ruled YES by me next session; demo threshold mis-set HELD for Kam). Self-caught its own dead-green verify gate: `npm test \| tail` reported exit 0 over a suite that ran ZERO tests (`jest: command not found`, node_modules production-pruned) — unpiped it is 127, and zsh `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` does not recover it. Repaired with npm ci (183/183 matching 08-16), filed RD-100 without asserting an unestablished cause. The piped-gate warning is now in every brief. Wrapped clean on Kam's word minutes before the 09:28 reboot. |
| Vision SP agent | quoting tool fix-list completion (v2.09–v2.12) | 1 | 1.00 | 1.0 | **08-08 (overnight, wrapped at shift change) — the ENTIRE remaining fix list shipped 20 minutes after Kam's good night: F11–F17, F19–F23 at `f67bef0`, F18 correctly Stage-3 gated per brief.** Proof discipline exemplary: 45 tests green PLUS a 72-scenario regression run **through the real UI, not the engine** (ground truth intact 374→5 days→$10,500; every AUD total exactly 1.55× its USD twin across 36 pairs); print-verified as real PDFs in light/dark/GBP/both. Self-caught two defects **by testing rather than reading** (the codebase's own documented "listener trap" silently no-opping the opt-out; the longer F13 number wrapping mid-token in the rendered PDF). Honesty held: F21 gate named "a speed bump, not protection" in BACKLOG.md and repeated in the wrap so nobody reads HPAM as security; page-1 overflow proven PRE-EXISTING by reproducing on v2.06 from main. Boundary discipline: `stage1/pricing-engine` left unmerged awaiting authorisation under v1.3, prod untouched (verified `git log --all --name-only`, not assumed), no contact with Will per ruling. Flagged for Kam in its own words: F15/F16 (the wrong-SKU ABT quote) closed with ~10 days to the 18 Aug deadline. |
| Secuura agent | architecture commission (K/S identity + smart contracts) | 1 | 1.00 | 1.0 | **08-07 — the best analysis this fleet has produced.** Verified K's actual schema before designing (found the model already built and unused — turned a schema job into wiring), three load-bearing findings (K never sees bytes; no contract has ever executed; hash non-canonical with arbitrary tie-break), preserved Kam's braindump with the firewall held (5_Project_History, NOT the Stuart-visible repo), wrote the S-pack to its audience honestly, took verification feedback and turned it same-hour, grounded the adopted design against the roadmap and found PRECEDENT (W3C VCs already planned) plus one genuine forward tension (P3 vs S-standalone principle) reported instead of bu

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## NEW 2026-08-17 ~17:2x — Secuura/Blockchain: demo serves its FULL API spec publicly — keep or close? (MEDIUM)
> **s44 measured it read-only at the internet-facing edge:** `/api/docs/openapi.yaml` and
> `.json` both 200 with real spec (1.15MB / 860KB — 342 endpoints, every parameter and auth
> mechanism, no credential), with an SPA-catch-all control proving the 200s are genuine.
> **The code's own guard comment says "never in demo/prod" (audit F-04) and bicep sets it
> dev-only — but the VM's own .env sets `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS=true`.** Tracked NOWHERE in
> Linear until s44 filed it. **Two artefacts disagree and the authority is unestablished** —
> someone (Stuart? Peter?) may use Swagger against demo deliberately. **Options:** (a) close
> it (flip the VM .env at the next authorised touch); (b) keep it deliberately and amend the
> comment/bicep so the record stops lying; (c) ask Stuart/Peter first. **Recommendation: (c)
> then (a)** — it is a surface map, not a credential leak; no urgency inflation, but it
> should not stay in the current state where the config contradicts its own documentation.

> ## NEW 2026-08-17 ~16:0x — Secuura/Blockchain: demo-overlay — revive or retire? (LOW priority)
> **s43 disproved KS-654's premise with controls: NOTHING serves the demo-overlay bundle** —
> the nginx `location /demo-overlay/` + `sub_filter` blocks were deliberately removed (the
> conf's own comment: "no functional value... visible errors on every page load"), the
> bind-mount was inert on BOTH targets, and the build had been broken 33 days with nobody
> noticing. The hygiene half is done (lockfile + a build that can go red + the dead mount
> deleted). **The product question remains: revive the overlay (restore serving) or retire it
> (delete the frontend)?** **Recommendation: RETIRE** — a feature nobody missed for a month is
> telling us its value. Nothing hangs on this; rule it whenever convenient.

> ## NEW 2026-08-17 ~14:1x — S
